tiles.heading: 01 · WET-BANK GROWTH
tiles.details: Compare the wet-bank growth habit in panel 0 with the separately archived, source-identified excavated root crown and long rhizomes in panel 13 (Romain Néron, IRIIS). The root photograph is not a Hays County voucher and is not traced to the flowering panicle in panel 1; a same-plant Hays-area root-to-head photograph is still missing.
tiles.short: Rhizomatous perennial with rough leaves and an open panicle
tiles.status: ARCHIVED ROOT/RHIZOME PHOTO — CONNECTED HAYS ROOT-TO-PANICLE VOUCHER MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · SHARP LEAF EDGE
tiles.details: Panel 12 (Larry Allain, USGS public domain) shows the actual leaf-blade edge at ordinary photo scale; panel 4 shows microscopic backward-curved prickles on the SHEATH, not the blade. Neither establishes the direction or size of individual BLADE-margin teeth. A taxon-confirmed 10–20× blade-edge macro with a 1-mm reference remains required; never feel the sharp edge with bare fingers.
tiles.short: Look for backward-pointing microscopic blade-margin teeth — never feel with bare fingers

tiles.heading: 03 · LOWEST PANICLE NODE
tiles.details: Rice cutgrass often has two or more primary branches at the lowest panicle node; white cutgrass often has one. Panel 1 now has a verified arrow to the LOWEST VISIBLE BRANCHING ZONE, but the source photograph does NOT resolve whether two branches actually originate from one node. Photograph the common attachment in front and side views; crossing branches are not a count.
tiles.short: Count branches sharing the lowest flowering-head node

tiles.heading: 04 · TRUE LIGULE
tiles.details: Panel 5 (Stefan.lefnaer sl23, CC BY-SA 4.0) actually shows the pale membranous ligule and an original printed 5-mm reference bar; the existing arrow identifies the visible flap. Published ligule length is roughly 0.5–1.5 mm (some treatments 0.5–1 mm), but the free apex and exact individual length are NOT independently measurable from this view. Obtain a perpendicular opened collar macro with 1-mm divisions; panel 3 is a hairy STEM NODE, not a ligule.
tiles.short: A real membranous ligule is photographed with a 5-mm scale; its free apex still needs measurement
tiles.status: TRUE LIGULE AND 5-MM BAR PHOTOGRAPHED — FREE APEX / 1-MM MEASUREMENT HOLD

tiles.heading: 05 · ONE-FLOWERED RICE SPIKELET
tiles.details: Panels 8 and 11 show actual detached source-identified spikelets with original 3-mm and 5-mm bars; panel 10 shows spikelet edges with a 10-mm bar, and panel 7 carries the photographer's Lem/Pal labels. Panel 15 is a single isolated flattened spikelet without a ruler. These photographs support anatomy and relative scale, NOT a measured 4.2–6.5 mm individual, independently confirmed absent/reduced basal glumes, or the same-specimen lemma/palea boundary. Do not invent glume arrows or a species measurement from a printed bar alone.
tiles.short: Scaled flattened spikelet photos exist; verify actual glumeless insertion and lemma/palea
tiles.status: SOURCE-LABELED SCALED SPIKELET VIEWS — GLUMELESS BASE / INDIVIDUAL MEASUREMENT HOLD

tiles.heading: 06 · RULE OUT WHITE CUTGRASS
tiles.details: Leersia virginica often has one lowest primary panicle branch and smaller approximately 2.2–4 mm spikelets; overlap and obscured attachments mean no single clue confirms either species. L. lenticularis has broader lentil-like spikelets. Keep protected Texas wild-rice and other wetland grasses undisturbed.
tiles.short: Combine lowest-branch count, spikelet size and leaf-edge anatomy
tiles.status: TEXT COMPARISON — MATCHED VERIFIED MACROS MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: RICE CUTGRASS: on wet stream edges inspect a source-verified airy loose panicle of narrow rice-grain spikelets plus rough grass blades. Use a lens, NEVER run bare fingertips along edges: backward-pointing sharp tiny LEAF-MARGIN teeth need their own 10–20× measured macro. Actual newly sourced photos show a HAIRY CULM NODE (not ligule), ROUGH SHEATH, REAL BLADE–SHEATH LIGULE, full inflorescence and a true opened one-flowered SPIKELET with lemma and palea. For white cutgrass L. virginica check the lowest branch junction (L. oryzoides frequently ≥2 branches) and mature ~4–6.5-mm spikelets rather than relying on wetland habitat. Austrian external photos are not independent Hays vouchers.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: Photograph a Hays-area wet-site culm from rooted base to its attached flowering panicle. The full gallery already contains a genuine separately excavated rice-cutgrass root crown and rhizomes, but it is not a connected Hays specimen.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Panel 12 (Larry Allain, USGS public domain) shows the actual leaf-blade edge at ordinary photo scale; panel 4 shows microscopic backward-curved prickles on the SHEATH, not the blade. Neither establishes the direction or size of individual BLADE-margin teeth. A taxon-confirmed 10–20× blade-edge macro with a 1-mm reference remains required; never feel the sharp edge with bare fingers.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Rice cutgrass often has two or more primary branches at the lowest panicle node; white cutgrass often has one. Panel 1 now has a verified arrow to the LOWEST VISIBLE BRANCHING ZONE, but the source photograph does NOT resolve whether two branches actually originate from one node. Photograph the common attachment in front and side views; crossing branches are not a count.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Rice cutgrass L. oryzoides: notably retrorse-prickly/rough leaves and sheaths; mature spreading panicle usually 2+ branches at lowermost nodes (verify their COMMON point on rachis); oblong flat 1-flowered spikelets usually 4.2–6.5 × 1.3–1.7 mm and short membranous ligule 0.5–1 mm. White cutgrass L. virginica: usually smoother or less harshly rough sheaths, often a single panicle branch at a lowermost node, smaller spikelets ~2.2–4 mm that generally overlap little along the branchlets (in contrast to the more overlapping spikelets of L. oryzoides); count mature branching and measure spikelets rather than rely on roughness. L. lenticularis has wider, almost disk- or lens-shaped spikelets, not narrow 'rice grains'. Zizaniopsis and Zizania have different flowering structure; Texas wild-rice is a protected aquatic plant and must not be handled or uprooted for comparisons. Paspalum spikelets are generally arranged differently; inspect the actual glumes/lemmas, not just habitat.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

memory_rule: LOOK without rubbing skin: rough backward-pointing LEAF MARGIN needs a macro; rough SHEATH plus a HAIRY STEM NODE + true LIGULE + OPEN 2+ branch base + RICE-SHAPED SPIKELETS. Opened spikelet has Lem + Pal, not obvious ordinary grass glumes.
safety_note: The archived IRIIS root/rhizome photograph is real and useful, but is not a Hays-area root-to-flowering-head voucher. The USGS blade-edge photo shows edge context, not independently direction-proven 10–20× teeth. Photo 2's broad leaves may belong to neighboring grass stems. No existing photograph proves 2+ branches co-originating at the lowest panicle node, the actual glumeless insertion, or an individually measured ligule. Preserve Joey's source-specific rights hold and avoid touching sharp leaf edges with bare hands.
field_rule: Leaf-edge retrorse prickles + mature open panicle + typically 2+ branches at basal PANICLE nodes + narrow measured 4.2–6.5 mm spikelets strongly support L. oryzoides; no single one proves the species.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
